title: Transition from the Dialogue with Kaliyuga to the South Udasi

blocks.text: The page finishes the dialogue with Kaliyuga by contrasting destructive desire with the Guru's saving intent. Where the age wishes sinners to sink, Baba Nanak resolves to ferry the world across and refuses to abandon creation to corruption.

That conclusion immediately becomes a journey outward as the narrative opens the southern udasi. The page therefore serves as a hinge from debate into travel, showing that compassion must move from speech into pilgrimage and instruction.

Its damaged state obscured the transition, but the neighboring pages make the movement clear. A world in moral decline is answered not by withdrawal, but by Guru Nanak's decision to go forth and redeem.
